title: Local Code Index
goal: Build a local queryable code graph so AI coding agents can retrieve symbols, relationships, and impact context with fewer blind file reads.

primary_tools.name: codegraph
primary_tools.role: Local-first code-intelligence graph with Tree-sitter parsing, MCP exposure, and impact analysis

when_to_use: The project is large enough that repeated grep and file reads waste context.
You want an MCP-compatible local index for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or similar agents.
You need impact analysis before touching a symbol or workflow.
when_not_to_use: The language or framework is not supported well enough for meaningful indexing.
You need runtime traces or production telemetry rather than static relationships.

demo.notes: No third-party tool is executed. This fixture shows the expected shape of a local index impact query.

codex_prompt: Use the local code-index capability to inspect related symbols and impact radius before editing. Query the graph for callers, callees, entry points, and affected files, then produce a short implementation plan with verification commands.
verification: The output references concrete symbols and files.
The plan includes likely affected callers or consumers.
The agent still reads source files before editing.
The final change is verified by project tests.
risks: Static graphs can miss dynamic imports, reflection, generated code, or framework conventions.
Index freshness matters; stale indexes can mislead agents.
MCP setup should be explicit and reversible.
